title: Basic gameplay: piracy, mining and policing
status: Implementation handoff; not a claim of implemented behaviour
intent: Make ordinary space travel a coherent playable simulation: geography and government affect encounters; miners extract real cargo; police investigate attacks and pursue the actual offender, including NPCs.
tuning_notice: All new distances, probabilities, timers, yields and legal penalties below are initial project design choices, not historical Elite specifications. Distances are native simulation units, not light years. Tune against actual travel speeds without changing the acceptance rules.

coordination.dispatch_policy: Prefer Elite Coder 1 and Elite Coder 2. If both are busy and Mission researcher is free, assign it a bounded independent general coding package as well as mission work. Do not interrupt active mission delivery or duplicate a claimed package. Check actual availability before dispatch and record the new owner.
coordination.current_work: Finish the existing route-alternatives validation/release checkpoint. Queue this as the next coherent gameplay feature; independent pure modules can start earlier in isolated worktrees after the interface checkpoint is agreed.

packages.scope: Shared entity/combat/event contracts; lawful self-defence and bounty correction; station security; police dispatch and pursuit; authoritative simulation/save/targeting integration; final validation and release.
packages.file_boundary: Sole owner for this feature's changes to Game.swift, Geometry.swift, GameRuntime, save format, central damage/death handling and shared renderer/input adapters. New crime/security modules and focused tests also belong here. Coordinate paths with the mission engine owner before editing its branch or interfaces.

packages.scope: Geographic encounter director, ordinary traffic, pirate/miner intent, deterministic asteroid fields, extraction and typed cargo payload rules, focused module tests.
packages.file_boundary: Own new independent encounter/mining modules and their dedicated tests. Return spawn requests, intents and events through G1 contracts. Do not concurrently edit G1 central files; deliver the small integration requirements to G1 with the module checkpoint. Finish the route UI slice first.

packages.preferred_owner: Mission researcher when free and both coders busy
packages.scope: A separately claimed compatibility/regression package: mission-protected encounter admission, combat-event provenance, typed cargo identity, pause/time and save compatibility tests. May take a larger independent unclaimed module if capacity changes and orchestrator explicitly transfers ownership.
packages.file_boundary: Existing mission engine and docs/research remain mission-owned. General gameplay test files must be separate from G1/G2 tests. No second implementation of crime, traffic or mining, and no second release publisher.

integration_rules: Agree an immutable source checkpoint and shared interface shape before parallel implementation; use suitable isolated managed worktrees, not concurrent edits to the main checkout.
G1 owns integration and backlog/release records. A transferred package must be explicitly relinquished by its previous owner before the fallback worker starts.
Publish only completed coherent vertical slices. Do not release unused scaffolding or mark a module done until its real game path works.
Preserve current route selection/countdown contracts and mission engine physical-time/library exclusions. Add future calendar cancellation at the validated route commit point as already agreed.
Use concise completion/blocker handoffs rather than repeated unchanged status relays.

shared_contracts.implementation_note: These are semantic contracts; reuse equivalent existing types instead of introducing parallel abstractions. G1 supplies concrete Swift names and signatures at the interface checkpoint.
shared_contracts.entity_identity: Stable reference distinguishing player, station and NPC, with system/visit identity and monotonic entity ID. One simulation allocator; never reuse a destroyed ID within a visit or collide with mission IDs.
shared_contracts.npc_state: Role (trader, miner, pirate, police, escort, mission), independent legal record/bounty, combat intent and current target. Hostile-to-player is derived presentation/intent, never proof of criminality. Keep origin, destination and cargo manifest for targeting computer display.
shared_contracts.encounter_context: Immutable Sendable snapshot of system seed/government, common-frame station/planet/sun anchors, local ships, player, active budgets, protected mission entities and physical simulation time. Pure module outputs are SpawnRequest and NPCIntent; GameRuntime applies them.
shared_contracts.combat_incident: Stable incident ID, physical timestamp, source actor including original missile/bomb owner, victim, attack kind, first aggressor, original legal status, hit/launch/death outcome and position. Record provenance when the event occurs, not from later mutated hostility. Exactly one destruction/bounty/drop result per victim.
shared_contracts.damage_resolution: All player/NPC lasers, missiles and bombs use one attributed damage/death pipeline. Resolve nearest actual ray intersection and occlusion, including the station, rather than the first array entry. Removal/culling is not destruction. Incoming ECM destruction remains attributed to ordnance and does not award ship-kill bounty.
shared_contracts.cargo_payload: Stable commodity identifier, native quantity/unit, unique payload ID, source and optional mission ownership. Collection is an atomic transfer. Reuse the cargo model's unit-aware capacity logic; do not map all pods to Food or silently replace mission cargo.
shared_contracts.asteroid_state: Stable galaxy/system/field/rock ID, composition, extraction state and remaining yield. Scene admission/culling does not recreate ore. Persist depletion and live collectible identity through save/load; a new visit must not reset a mined rock.
simulation_rules: Swift 6 isolation: GameRuntime owns all mutable simulation; AppKit/UI remains on the main actor. Worker modules are pure or owned by the runtime, with Sendable data boundaries.
Use the existing physical simulation clock, with unchanged pause/title/library freeze policy. No timers driven by UI redraw or wall clock.
Use dedicated deterministic encounter and mining random streams, so adding population logic does not perturb mission randomness. Serialize their state if needed for save continuity.

Derive every region and field from the same scene coordinate frame; player rotation/translation must move anchors and bodies consistently. Do not mix camera-relative bodies with static world-coordinate zones.
Respect mission-owned spawn suppression and protected bodies. Global encounter admission uses one budget and prioritizes mission entities and station defence.

rules: An unlawful attack is recorded on the first verified hit or targeted missile attack, not only on a kill. Victim retaliation never changes the original offence or awards a clean-victim bounty.
A victim may defend against its recorded unlawful aggressor without gaining a crime. This right ends when the threat ends and does not authorize attacks on unrelated ships.
Attacking a known wanted criminal is lawful outside the station no-fire zone. Station no-fire policy is separate from bounty legality; immediate self-defence is allowed within it.
Police must investigate the actual first aggressor, whether player or NPC. Existing player legal values and Clean/Offender/Fugitive thresholds remain compatible.

An unobserved deep-space attack causes local defence/distress, not an instant omniscient station response. Station sensors or a nearby police witness can report it; civilian distress reaches authority only within the station relay zone.
A genuine hit on the station triggers an alarm even if its hull is invulnerable. Lasers and missiles must not silently skip the station. Ordinary collision is not automatically intentional assault.
A missed shot inside the no-fire zone produces a first warning; another discharge within 10 physical seconds creates a no-fire incident. Outside it, an unaimed missed shot is not assault.
Bounty requires a pre-existing legal bounty/mission entitlement and lawful kill credit; the hostile flag alone grants nothing. Preserve explicit mission rewards with exactly-once settlement.

initial_penalties.deduplication: Apply one assault offence per actor/victim encounter within a rolling 10-second attack window, not per laser frame. Continuous hits extend the window. Murder adds its one death penalty; specialized police/station offence replaces generic assault rather than stacking both. Save/load preserves recent active incidents.

dispatch.ordinary_report: Dispatch up to 2 available Vipers after 4-8 simulation seconds, faster in lawful governments. If already present, patrols respond immediately to a verified threat and physically fly to it.
dispatch.station_attack: First wave of 3 Vipers begins after 4 seconds. Add up to 2 every 10 seconds while the attack remains active, with at most 8 active police. Repeated hits update the same alarm; no unbounded launch loop.
dispatch.launch: Ships appear at the actual station exit with separation and safe launch headings, then intercept the offender; they do not teleport onto it. Reserve admission capacity for defence.
dispatch.priorities: Active station attacker, active unlawful attacker threatening a clean victim, known fugitive, known offender. Recheck live target identity, offence and line of fire before each attack. Do not shoot through clean traffic.
dispatch.government: Lawful systems have more patrols and faster reporting. Anarchy has no routine authority patrol, but its station still defends itself when attacked.
dispatch.deescalation: After 30 seconds without new violence, clear active alarm into cooldown once the threat is gone or outside dispatch range. A police pursuit searches after losing contact and returns after 60 seconds without reacquisition or outside a 20000-unit station leash. Legal record persists; retreat does not erase the offence.
dispatch.docking: Deny docking during an active security alarm against the player or while a known fugitive. Allow ordinary offender docking when not in active pursuit, with a warning. Targeting-computer autodock aborts visibly/with voice when permission is denied; it must not loop against the entrance.
dispatch.player_protection: A clean player attacked within detection range automatically reports the incident; police pursue the attacker without extra equipment. Legal police action against a wanted player is not treated as an attack on a clean victim.

crime_and_security.presentation: Use existing compact HUD text and voice event queue: 'Weapons prohibited near station', 'Unlawful attack recorded', 'Distress received; police responding', 'Station under attack; security launching', 'Docking permission denied'. Name the culprit in the details. Announce state changes once; throttle repeats. Preserve the user's requirement that on-screen notifications are also voiced.

traffic_and_piracy.regions: Station approach/exit traffic; station-to-arrival/planet trade lanes; outer planet-to-star mining band; deep space outside the lanes. Classify using anchor distances and distance to lane segments rather than forward-screen position.
encounters: Reassess local population every seeded 8-12 physical seconds. These weights affect population admission, not a guaranteed attack on every interval.
Ordinary pirate packs have 1-3 ships; high-pressure anarchic/feudal encounters can have 2-5. Deep space is sparse but supports occasional packs. Corporate deep space has a small nonzero risk.

Pirates prefer valuable cargo carriers, including NPC traders; they intercept, engage and collect dropped goods. They flee police superiority or hull/energy below 25%. No requirement to add cargo-demand dialogue for this slice.

Traders fly between actual arrival points and station approaches, avoiding no-fire violence and sending distress. Miners travel to fields and extract shared rocks. Ships have valid origin/destination data.
NPC intent supports NPC targets and normal orientation, range, cooldown and occlusion rules. Replace player-only hostile damage shortcuts through G1 integration.

Spawn at valid traffic entries or outside immediate perception with safe separation; never materialize an attacker in point-blank view. Return/cull ordinary actors only outside perception, without reporting a kill or removing protected mission entities.

population_budget.policy: Single G1 allocator enforces combined ordinary admission, reserving at least 8 places for police and 4 for mission requests before accepting ambient work. Mission entities and protected payloads must never be dropped to meet ordinary caps. Reconcile exceptional scripted encounter budgets with mission owner, rather than truncating the mission. Validate performance on the final active-body budget.

fields.placement: Seed by galaxy/system/field identity. Use the outer planet-to-star band, excluding the station security zone, planet interior and its 2-radius safety margin, and the sun's 4-radius heat envelope. Generate a deterministic safe offset/fallback when the line segment is too short. Fields must be reachable and visible through the navigation/scanner, not confined to a launch asteroid.

loop: Fly to a labelled 'Mining field' beacon on the existing navigation/scanner presentation. Show distance and do not require a new prospector item.

Aim an installed Mining Laser on any supported facing at a rock. Use existing laser damage and a 100-200 energy rock range so ordinary mining takes roughly 2-4 mining hits; extraction happens once at depletion.
Mining Laser releases typed collectible fragments with modest outward velocity. Other lasers and bombs can destroy rocks but yield no valuable ore, making the mining equipment meaningful.
Use the existing fuel-scoop approach and collision rules for collection. Without scoops, no collection. Capacity refusal leaves the fragment intact, with a throttled 'Cargo hold full' message.

Collection transfers the actual payload and unit into cargo, then removes the fragment exactly once. Partial collection, if supported by the current cargo engine, must retain the precise remainder; otherwise collect atomically only when it fits.

NPC miners and player share the same depletion ledger. Culling, changing view, docking, revisiting and save/load cannot create another yield from an already mined rock. Persist pending collectible payloads or explicitly expire them without regenerating them.
Ordinary trader wreck cargo uses its real seeded manifest and cannot duplicate existing mission/scripted loot. Mission payloads retain their identity and settlement rules.

initial_yield.base: 1-5 tonnes of Minerals per mined rock, emitted in small collectible pods.
initial_yield.precious: 1 kilogram of Gold or Platinum, chosen deterministically; never interpret it as a tonne.

mining.presentation: Show field name/range, ore payload identity and collected quantity. Use the existing commodity colours and the compact fixed font at all window sizes. Voice collection/full-hold messages through the same deduplicated event queue.

compatibility: Keep normal and XYZZY behaviour consistent; existing invulnerability/unlimited cargo affect outcomes but do not disable incidents, witnesses, NPC interaction or field generation. Validate capacity and combat scenarios with cheats disabled.
Old saves supply safe defaults for new roles, records, incident state and field ledgers. Do not reset cash, equipment, legal status, galaxy, mission progress or active route.
Do not activate or rewrite the separate mission engine as a side effect. Ask its owner to reconcile protected IDs, source-attributed deaths, custody, event history and physical time interfaces.
Mission deaths/rewards/cargo collection remain exactly once. Preserve Naval/Constrictor/plans, Blackjack and scripted spawn suppression; ambient police must not hijack reserved mission entities.

Destroying the player's selected target reports player kill credit when appropriate, not 'Target lost'; culling/lost contact remains distinct. Preserve military targeting/ECM retaliation without introducing crimes from misattributed ordnance.
No fines payment, reputation economy, boarding, full-galaxy offline simulation or new mandatory equipment is needed for this slice.

acceptance.scenario: Laser-hit a clean ship near station: offence appears on first hit, police target player, victim retaliation cannot erase crime and its destruction gives no generic hostile bounty.
Repeat A01 with player missile and bomb. Original shooter survives ordnance/ECM transitions in provenance, with no duplicate penalty or death reward.
Clean player defends against a pirate: no assault/murder charge; lawful bounty is credited once. An unrelated clean ship remains protected.
Pirate attacks clean player or NPC trader near station: distress/report yields delayed police help targeting the pirate, with NPC-versus-NPC combat.
Shoot station with laser/missile: hit is detected, alarm is voiced/displayed, first 3 Vipers launch after delay and later waves respect the active cap.
Continuous station fire does not launch a wave per frame or stack generic and station assault. Retreat clears alarm after quiet/leash rules but preserves legal record.
Unwitnessed deep-space assault causes local defence but no immediate remote police. The same attack in sensor/witness range is reported.
A fugitive NPC is pursued by patrols; a clean bystander is not. Reacquisition, lost contact, return and docking denial do not loop or target a recycled ID.
First missed discharge in no-fire zone warns; repeated discharge violates. Lawful bounty hunting outside zone and immediate self-defence inside are correctly distinguished.
Nearest ray intersection and station occlusion prevent hitting a farther clean/pirate target through an intervening object.
Seeded encounter samples show higher pirate pressure in anarchy than corporate, lower station than lane pressure, and occasional deep-space pirates in lawful systems.
Traffic follows real routes, pirates attack NPC cargo carriers and flee overwhelming police; no forced player combat each spawn interval.
Rotate/translate player: field anchors and zone membership remain physically consistent. Fields lie in the safe planet-to-star band and can be reached in normal play.
Mining laser on each supported facing extracts ore; ordinary laser/bomb destroys without valuable yield. Two resolution calls produce one yield.
Scoop Minerals, Alloys and rare kilogram payloads into correct commodity/unit quantities. Without scoops or with full hold, fragment remains collectible.
Player/NPC race to the same rock or fragment; one extraction/collection succeeds. Culling/revisit/save reload preserves depletion and cannot farm duplicate ore.
Ambient admission preserves police reserve, bounded counts and mission requests. Culling never increments kills or settles mission rewards.
Old/new save round trips preserve cash/equipment/legal/route/mission state; reload does not erase a station offence or clone live loot.
Pause/title/library and other physical-time exclusions stay compatible; simulated time partition/frame rate does not change encounter decisions, timers or yields.
Existing mission combat/custody/reward events pass regression tests; new encounter random draws do not alter mission random sequences.
Normal and XYZZY live play show the same ecology; HUD/voice state changes are understandable, bounded and use the fixed small font at full screen.

sequence: Implement G1 incident/damage/security and G2 traffic/mining concurrently in separate files
Integrate through the G1 runtime adapters
Execute the real-game scenarios and mission compatibility checks
Validate one settled feature checkpoint and publish through the existing release owner
delivery.required_checks: Focused deterministic regression tests per package, native game smoke scenarios with rendered evidence, then make ci for coverage, sanitizer and leak gates on the integrated checkpoint. Do not report CI from an earlier SHA as evidence for later edits.
delivery.publication: G1 maintains backlog, README/help and required issue/PR handoffs; no automatic release version assumed by this design. Sonar analysis only on committed main, exact lowercase 40-character SHA as projectVersion. README media only make readme-media. Preserve signed/notarized macOS distribution workflow and protected publication policy.
delivery.definition_of_done: All six requested gameplay behaviours are reachable in the ordinary game, tests and native evidence pass, and owners report the actual integrated source checkpoint and any remaining limitations. A pure helper module without game wiring is not complete.
